reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of FGM is that standard graphical models fail when forecast errors are driven by shared factors, because such structures induce dense correlations among error terms—violating the sparsity assumption underlying GLASSO. This leads to degenerate estimates where all partial correlations collapse to zero. FGM addresses this by first residualizing errors using an approximate factor model, thereby isolating idiosyncratic components that are plausibly sparse. Then, it applies graphical modeling techniques (e.g., GLASSO) to these residuals to estimate their precision matrix. Finally, it reconstructs the full precision matrix using the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury identity, which combines the estimated idiosyncratic precision with the factor structure. This approach ensures both theoretical consistency of the weight estimates and practical superiority in forecasting accuracy, especially at longer horizons. The failure mode of plain GLASSO is thus identified and mitigated through a structured decomposition of the error process.
